name: When do I need custom framing instead of standard framing for an addition?

mainEntity.name: When do I need custom framing instead of standard framing for an addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need custom framing when your addition incorporates non-standard architectural elements, such as vaulted or coffered ceilings, pocket doors, enlarged window openings, or uneven rooflines. Standard framing techniques handle basic box additions, but custom framing is required whenever you alter exterior load-bearing walls or match vintage room proportions in established neighborhoods around Denver or Greenwood Village. Custom framing also includes adding blocking for heavy floating vanities, specialized accessibility grab bars, or built-in shelving, ensuring your wall studs are reinforced for specific interior plans.
acceptedAnswer.description: Custom framing is needed for vaulted ceilings, large structural openings, roof transitions, and adding specific wall blocking for cabinets, trim, or grab bars.
